newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh border security forces have beefed up patrolling along the Burmese border to prevent the fresh influx of Rohingya muslim refugees.
The Unites States Agency for International development (USAID) will finance a Tk 8.82 billion health project providing "one stop" service to improve the health of mothers and children in Bangladesh.
Authorities on Tuesday restored rail links between eastern Sylhet district and other parts of the country which had been cut off following a gas filed fire middle of last month.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, now visiting Japan, is scheduled to meet her Japanese counterpart Ryutaro Hashimoto on Wednesday for official talks.
Bangladesh and Japan on Tuesday signed an agreement on the protection and promotion of investment.
Bangladesh will receive loans amounting 15.25 billion Yen from Japan under three separate agreements signed in Tokyo on Tuesday.
The work for development of Korean Export Processing Zone in Chittagong will begin in October.
A World Bank study says that South Asia's textile output will increase 17 percent, and exports 26 percent as a result of phase out of the Multi Fibre Arrangement (MFA). REUTER
